title: Synchronize reserved-capacity quota windowing and implement backfill for missed resets
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Reserved capacity customers currently experience mismatched quota resets across hosted and dedicated deployments and between regions. This causes transient double-billing or lost burst credits when a tenant's reset event is processed out-of-order (clock skew, delayed ledger writes, or cross-region replay). Goal: implement a deterministic, idempotent window synchronization mechanism plus a backfill process to reconcile missed or delayed resets for reserved-capacity quota buckets without impacting live SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: All reserved-capacity tenants receive consistent daily and monthly quota boundaries across regions within a 60s convergence window
Automated backfill reconciles missed resets for up to 72 hours of delayed events and writes an auditable ledger entry for each adjustment
No customer sees transient negative available_quota values; billing ledger balances remain non-negative
Migration can be rolled back via feature flag and manual reset API without data loss
Integration tests covering clock-skew, replayed events, and cross-region leader failover added to CI
implementation_notes: Introduce a reset_epoch field (ISO8601 UTC) on quota buckets; leaders publish authoritative epoch for each tenant and window type
Use vector-clock-like monotonic token (tenant_reset_id) to ensure idempotent processing across shards
Backfill processor consumes delayed reset events from the event-store (Kafka topic) and emits adjustment deltas to the billing ledger; adjustments are tagged with original_event_ts and processed_by
Edge case: tenants with simultaneous dedicated and hosted allocations must be handled by unified router to prevent double-decrements; plan adds per-tenant routing table check during reset operation
Add an escape-hatch admin API (/admin/quotas/:tenant_id/reset) with audit log and RBAC for manual reconciliation
Metrics: publish reset_processed_latency, backfill_adjustments_count, ledger_mismatch_rate, and reset_conflict_rate to billing dashboards
test_plan: Unit tests for idempotency: process same reset_event twice, ledger delta applied only once
Integration test in staging with simulated 30s clock skew between region-primary and region-secondary
Chaos test: kill leader during reset window and verify follower completes deterministic epoch publish
Load test: run reset flow across 10k tenants concurrently to verify <500ms median reset processing and no SLO regression
Manual verification steps for canary tenants and sample ledger reconciliation queries
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated rollout: start with <=20 tenants in dedicated pool (canary) for 48 hours
If no anomalies, expand to 1% of tenants for 24h, then 10% for 48h, then global
Monitor ledger_mismatch_rate and customer_error_reports during each phase
Provide a one-click rollback via admin console and a scripted manual backfill as fallback
mitigations_and_risks: Risk: Backfill races with live consumption leading to temporary over-crediting. Mitigation: apply adjustments as non-consumable pending credits until reconciled in ledger commit phase
Risk: Large-scale backfills overload ledger writer. Mitigation: implement rate-limited batching and priority queue with per-tenant rate caps
Risk: Clock skew > configured threshold. Mitigation: reject direct reset events and surface to ops for manual review; use event-store replay with monotonic tenant_reset_id
